messages.content:
Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 30
  gender: Female
  ethnicity: Middle Eastern
  relationship_status: Divorced
  occupation: Bartender
  trauma_type: Witnessed domestic violence (childhood)
  pcl5: 61

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Maladaptive Strategies: Worst Case Rehearsal: mentally rehearse worst case scenarios to feel prepared, Avoid Open Spaces: Open or exposed spaces where I feel vulnerable, Emotion Control: I try hard to control my emotions
  Threat: Threat in Movements: Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard, Safe Zone Only: I only feel safe in a very limited number of places, Door and Lock Checking: I repeatedly check that doors and windows are locked
  Memory: Overwhelm on Recall: When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop, Nonverbal Memory: I can't seem to put the frightening event into words., Cannot Find Words: I know what happened but I am unable to find words to describe it
  Negative Appraisals: Can't Rely on Self: I can't rely on myself, Self-Doubt: I can't trust that I will do the right thing, Mistrust: People can't be trusted

Vignette:
Layla, a 30-year-old Middle Eastern woman, has been struggling with the aftermath of witnessing domestic violence during her childhood. Her early experiences have left indelible marks on her psyche, shaping how she navigates the world today. Layla is divorced and currently works as a bartender at a local restaurant in a bustling city neighborhood. The traumatic event that haunts Layla occurred when she was just 10 years old. She remembers vividly the night her father, intoxicated and enraged, stormed into their home, his movements sudden and unpredictable. Her mother tried to calm him down but he lashed out physically. In those moments of chaos and fear, Layla found herself paralyzed with terror, unable to process or articulate what was happening around her. This event has shaped how she perceives threats today. Sudden movements by others instantly put her on high alert; the mere sight of a person's quick gesture can trigger an overwhelming surge of anxiety. She often finds herself mentally rehearsing worst-case scenarios, trying to prepare for any possible danger that might arise. This mental rehearsal is both a coping mechanism and a source of distress, as it leaves her feeling perpetually on edge. Layla’s sense of safety is confined to a very limited number of places she deems secure. Her home, where she can lock the doors and windows multiple times, is one such sanctuary. Outside this safe zone, Layla feels intensely vulnerable. The open spaces at her workplace, with its large windows and bustling customers, are particularly challenging for her. She has developed a habit of avoiding those areas as much as possible, which sometimes means taking less desirable shifts that are tucked away in the back of the bar. The memory of that night is seared into Layla’s mind, but it resists verbalization. When she tries to recall and describe what happened, she finds herself unable to find words to convey her experience fully. The emotions associated with this event overwhelm her whenever the memories surface. She often isolates herself when these thoughts come flooding back, as they are too intense to bear in public. Layla’s negative appraisals have deeply impacted her self-perception and relationships. She struggles with feelings of self-doubt, believing that she can't rely on herself to make sound decisions or handle challenging situations effectively. This mistrust extends beyond herself; she finds it difficult to trust others as well. The incidents from her childhood have left a lasting impression that people cannot be trusted, making forming new connections and maintaining relationships particularly arduous. Her occupation as a bartender has been affected by these fears. She avoids engaging with customers in open areas of the bar where she feels exposed. Over time, this avoidance has led to some tension with her coworkers who often misunderstand her behavior as aloofness or lack of interest. Layla’s colleagues have noticed that she frequently checks the locks on doors and windows at work, which sometimes makes them question her reliability. Layla finally decided to seek help after a particularly distressing episode at work where a sudden movement by a customer triggered intense panic and led to a minor accident with a glass. She was shaken and recognized that these reactions were interfering significantly with her life and job performance. What frightens her most is the fear of being overwhelmed again, unable to control her emotions or react appropriately in critical moments. At the same time, Layla hopes for a sense of stability and security. She wants to be able to navigate her daily life without feeling constantly on guard and to trust herself and others more fully. Seeking therapy represents a significant step towards reclaiming some measure of control over her life and addressing the lingering effects of her childhood trauma.
